overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to review executive session minutes at reasonable intervals; the violation was not found intentional, the minutes-request claim was declined as a Public Records Law matter, and remedial orders issued.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to review executive session minutes at reasonable intervals to decide whether continued nondisclosure was warranted.
allegations.key_passage: We find that in failing to perform the required review of executive session minutes, the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to review executive session minutes in response to his request for them; AG found the request fell under the Public Records Law.
allegations.key_passage: As the complainant's request was directed to the town clerk only, without any indication that it was intended for the Board or any request that it be forwarded to the Board, we find that the request was made under the Public Records Law, not the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Create and approve accurate minutes of all executive sessions held before July 16, through whatever means are available, including attendees' memories and notes (to the extent not already done).
Review for release all existing executive session minutes not reviewed within the last six months, and announce the results at the next open session, recording them in those minutes.
Certify compliance to the AG within 60 days of receipt; if minutes cannot be created despite best efforts, explain in writing within 60 days what efforts were made.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: To the extent that it has not already done so, we order the Board to create and approve accurate minutes of all executive session meetings that took place prior to the date the complaint was filed with the Board, July 16, through whatever means are available, including the memories and individual notations of the attendees.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
